s0401.literal: As for securing the state and nurturing the people, fundamentally it follows the will of the myriad things; timely riding and governing
s0401.idiomatic: To secure the realm and cherish the people rests on the will of all under Heaven; to ride the times and steer the state

s0403.literal: [Yu], Editorial footnote marker 42. a heart meeting at the right moment for joyous yielding.
s0403.idiomatic: [Yu], See editorial note 42. the heart of the age ready to yield the throne in glad accord.

s0404.literal: Seven hundred years have no fixed term; kings and emperors are not of one clan. Formerly when the Wood Virtue had reached its end, the mandate passed to our Liang; Heaven's sequence truly gathers upon the wise and clear.
s0404.idiomatic: Seven hundred years know no fixed span, and royal lines are not one house. When the Wood Virtue waned, the mandate came to our Liang; Heaven's count now settles on the wise.

s0405.literal: Following the former canon, broadly consulting collective deliberation, kings, dukes, ministers, and prefects—none failed to attach themselves; respectfully following the wish of human spirits, we confer the imperial seat upon your person.
s0405.idiomatic: In accord with ancient precedent, after wide counsel among lords and ministers, all attached to this course; honoring the people's wish, we place the imperial throne in your hands.

s0406.literal: The four seas are impoverished and exhausted; Heaven's bounty ends forever. O King, earnestly hold the center, follow the models of old, to fulfill the hope of all beneath Heaven!
s0406.idiomatic: The realm is spent and Heaven's favor has run its course. Hold the Mean, follow the old patterns, and answer what all under Heaven expects of you!

s0407.literal: In suburban sacrifice to the Supreme Lord, timely receive the great rites, forever secure the vast enterprise—is it not magnificent!
s0407.idiomatic: Sacrifice to Heaven, receive the great rites in season, and make the great enterprise endure—what glory could be greater!

s0408.literal: An edict by imperial seal also said:

s0409.literal: The gentleman brightens his own virtue; the man of attainment is ahead of Heaven and does not violate it—therefore in advance and retreat all is penetrating, in movement and stillness primordially auspicious.
s0409.idiomatic: The gentleman makes his virtue shine; the sage anticipates Heaven and does not oppose it—so whether he advances or withdraws all goes well, and in action or repose he is fundamentally blessed.

s0410.literal: Though We are shallow and few, We are perhaps not far from that lofty conduct.
s0410.idiomatic: Though We are dull and slight, We may yet approach that high example.

s0412.literal: When the three powers were divided and the nine domains distinguished, natures and dispositions diverged and disorder rose like clouds—therefore they established those who tend the people and promoted the sage and worthy; those who received and yielded took office as the time came; kings and emperors by origin were not one clan; human counsel agreed; one bent oneself to follow the heart of the myriad things; Heaven's intent thus returned; one bowed the body to serve the command of the hundred spirits.
s0412.idiomatic: Once heaven, earth, and man were set apart and the realm was carved into regions, hearts pulled apart and chaos spread—so rulers were appointed and sages raised up. Transfer of the mandate came when the time came; dynasties were not one bloodline. Where human counsel agreed, the throne bent to the people's will; where Heaven turned, the ruler bowed to the spirits.

s0413.literal: Where songs of acclaim went, one rolled up one's sleeves to receive it; when the essence was spent, one lifted one's robe and departed.
s0413.idiomatic: Where popular acclaim led, the ruler rolled up his sleeves and took the burden; when his virtue was spent, he gathered his robe and walked away.

s0414.literal: Formerly under Tang and Yu, taking Heaven's way as mirror, they raised the black-haired people and conferred it upon the wise and clear; though substance and pattern, writing and track differed and institutions changed with the age, through successive generations this wind never ceased.
s0414.idiomatic: In Tang and Yu times, mirroring Heaven, they chose the people and gave rule to the wise; forms and rites changed from age to age, yet the custom of yielding never died out.

s0415.literal: Our Great Liang therefore examined merit in the Grand Temple, received rites at the secondary palace, on the first day of the first month received the end from the civil ancestor.
s0415.idiomatic: Our Liang thus tested merit in the Grand Temple, received the rites at the secondary palace, and on New Year's Day took the mandate from the former sovereign.

s0416.literal: But fortune is not always level and the Way has no constant peace; mountains and hills toppled, rivers and seas seethed; birds with lightning eyes and thunder voices, beasts with hooked claws and saw teeth, chewed and devoured the living without knowing limit.
s0416.idiomatic: Yet fortune is not always smooth and the Way not always tranquil: mountains overturned and seas boiled; monstrous birds and savage beasts devoured life without end.

s0417.literal: The two sovereigns were heroic and sage, succeeding one another in Heaven; the six Yi were greedy and cunning and strove to invade the central land; men set up as kings and emperors harbored designs against the statutes; not one man or inch of soil was any longer Liang territory.
s0417.idiomatic: Two sage emperors followed one another in Heaven, yet the six barbarians clawed at the heartland; pretenders raised banners and men nursed treason; not a man or a foot of soil truly remained Liang ground.

s0418.literal: We, through misfortune, in youth met with bereavement, relying upward on balancing assistants; years swiftly shifted.
s0418.idiomatic: We, ill-fated, lost our father young and leaned on regents while the years hurried by.

s0419.literal: King Cheng of Zhou and Emperor Hui of Han—how far off, without a stair! Only this childish innocence was bound to bring downfall.
s0419.idiomatic: King Cheng of Zhou and Emperor Hui of Han are far beyond reach; this childish rule could only invite ruin.

s0420.literal: If the age had lacked a sage and the world had not known hardship, We would still have strode high on the blue isles and sought for Ourselves the path of Taibo.
s0420.idiomatic: Had there been no sage and no calamity, We would still have withdrawn to the marshes and sought Taibo's way of yielding.

s0421.literal: Only the King answered the age and was born outstanding, opened the register and grasped the chart; the Way and its teaching are therefore hard to hear of, fine merit already covers things; the Qian movement matches its sheltering canopy, the sun chariot compares to its steadfast brightness; he ascended to receive the sage's work of restoring Yu, set up the foster son in the enterprise of raising Zhou, destroyed Luhun at Yi and Luo, annihilated the Li Rong at Haojing; the fierce troops of the two Zhens great and small, the powerful foes of the two Yues southeast and southwest—suddenly Heaven's punishment was carried out, none missed by divine strategy.
s0421.idiomatic: But the King met his season, opened the mandate and held the chart; his virtue is hard to name and his merit already blankets the world. Like Heaven's canopy he shelters all; like the sun he shines steady. He took up Yu's restoration and Zhou's founding charge, crushed Luhun on the Yi and Luo and the Li Rong at Haojing, and swept the fierce hosts of the two Zhens and the strong rebels of the two Yues—Heaven's strike fell at once, nothing escaping his design.

s0422.literal: Thereupon he traced Yao and Shun and took Wen and Wu as model; great music harmonized with heaven and earth, great rites shared their seasons with heaven and earth; drummed with thunder, moistened with wind and rain; benevolence soaked the reeds, faith reached pigs and fish; the Yin window stood empty, the Xia tower was void; the people were greatly stored, in the wild there were fellows; the Ascendant Peace hymn was sung, without partiality or faction—firmly clouds flew over the purple canopy, the yellow dragon leapt in the waters; east campaign and west expedition gleamed across rivers and land; glory warmed and already overspread the suburbs; sweet dew dripped and repeatedly flowed through the palace gardens.
s0422.idiomatic: He took Yao and Shun as his model and Wen and Wu as his law; music and rites matched heaven and earth; thunder drummed and rain moistened; kindness reached the humblest grass, trust even to fish and swine; prisons stood empty and towers unused; the people flourished and harmony filled the land. Clouds crowned the purple canopy and dragons leapt in the waters; his armies flashed across the realm; glory bathed the suburbs and sweet dew drenched the palace courts.

s0423.literal: Cart ruts and horse tracks—who did not follow?
s0423.idiomatic: Cart tracks and hoofprints—who did not follow?

s0424.literal: Coiling waters and flowing sands—who did not cherish virtue?
s0424.idiomatic: From winding streams to shifting sands—who did not honor his virtue?

s0425.literal: Auspicious charts came from afar—not only the red talisman; the numinous mandate was clear—not only the yellow star's breath.
s0425.idiomatic: Portents arrived from afar, not only the red talisman of Liu Bang; Heaven's mandate was plain, not only the yellow star's omen.

s0426.literal: River mouth and river eyes—the sage's outward signs were already displayed; grasping the banner and holding the battle-axe—the ruler's form was thus grand.
s0426.idiomatic: The marks of a sage showed in his face; bearing banner and axe, he had the bearing of a true king.

s0427.literal: Moreover from the time Sheti lost its reckoning and Mengzou perished, the crooked arrow flew by night and the sky bow shone at dawn—long had the barbarian sheep been in the pastures; the hour had come for the flood dragon to rise from the spring.
s0427.idiomatic: Since the stars lost their order and the calendar broke down, comets crossed the night sky—barbarians had long overrun the fields; the time had come for the dragon to rise from the deep.

s0428.literal: Omens of a change in mandate were all manifest; tokens of renewal gathered thickly—We therefore revered Kun and Hua and repeatedly turned the star gauge.
s0428.idiomatic: Every sign of a new mandate appeared; tokens of renewal gathered—so We revered the models of Yao and Shun and long hesitated before Heaven's clock.

s0429.literal: Formerly when the Wood cycle was spent, Our High Ancestor received it.
s0429.idiomatic: When the Wood mandate ended, our founder received it.

s0430.literal: Now the calendar has left the Fire brilliance; the spirit returns to the pivot; respectfully with the Fire Virtue We transmit it to your Chen.
s0430.idiomatic: Now the Fire mandate has run its course and the spirit returns to the center; We respectfully pass the Fire mandate to your Chen.

s0431.literal: Looking far to former kings and consulting near with the hundred lords, the bright spirits are pleased and all within the seas share one heart.
s0431.idiomatic: Taking former kings as mirror and the hundred lords as counsel, the spirits approve and the realm is of one mind.

s0432.literal: Now We send envoys bearing credentials: concurrently Grand Mentor, Palace Attendant, Minister of the Masters of Writing, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Marquis of Pingle Precinct Wang Tong, Editorial footnote marker 43. and concurrently Grand Commandant, Director of the Masters of Writing, Left chief clerk Wang Chang to present the imperial seal and cord.
s0432.idiomatic: We now send envoys with credentials: Grand Mentor and Left Vice Director Wang Tong, See editorial note 43. and Grand Commandant chief clerk Wang Chang, to deliver the imperial seal and cord.

s0433.literal: The rites of receiving the end shall wholly follow the Tang and Yu precedents.
s0433.idiomatic: The abdication rites shall follow entirely the precedent of Tang and Yu.

s0434.literal: O King, at the proper time ascend as the primary consort, nurture and rear the hundred thousand people, broadly unfold the great design, to receive the felicitous mandate of august Heaven!
s0434.idiomatic: King, take the throne in due season, nurture the people, and unfold the great plan to receive Heaven's bright command!

s0435.literal: That day the Liang Emperor yielded the throne at a separate palace.
s0435.idiomatic: That day the Liang emperor abdicated to a side palace.

s0436.literal: The Founder declined again and again; the hosts of ministers firmly pressed him, and he then assented.
s0436.idiomatic: The Founder refused again and again until the ministers pressed him firmly, and then he accepted.

s0438.literal: Marquis of Xinyu Xiao Mo served as Administrator of Wuxing: "Xinyu" in the Biography of Du Sengming reads "Xinyu" (Yu with water radical); elsewhere Yu and Yu also appear interchangeably.
s0438.idiomatic: On "Marquis of Xinyu Xiao Mo, administrator of Wuxing": the Biography of Du Sengming writes Xinyu with the water radical; the speech and water forms interchange elsewhere.

s0439.literal: Comment: the "Yu" of "Xinyu" was originally written "Yu" (with water), named for the Yu River; after Tianbao of Tang the form "Yu" (with speech) was used in succession—see the Treatise on Geography in the Book of Tang and the Yuanhe Commanderies and Counties Gazetteer.
s0439.idiomatic: Note: Xinyu was originally written with the water radical for the Yu River; after Tang Tianbao the speech radical form became standard—see the Book of Tang geography treatise and the Yuanhe gazetteer.

s0440.literal: "Xiao Mo" in the Biography of Du Sengming reads "Xiao Ying"; elsewhere Mo and Ying also appear interchangeably; now Mo and Ying are treated as the same character and are not normalized to one form.
s0440.idiomatic: On "Xiao Mo": the Biography of Du Sengming reads Xiao Ying; Mo and Ying interchange elsewhere; the forms are treated as variants and not forced to one spelling.

s0441.literal: Jiaozhi rebelled and turned: "rebelled and turned" in all editions reads "rebelled and scattered."
s0441.idiomatic: On "Jiaozhi rebelled and turned": all editions read rebelled and scattered.

s0442.literal: Comment: rebelled-and-turned and rebelled-and-scattered are both reduplicative binomes; the sound is the same and the sense close. Where this book uses turn and scatter interchangeably there are several instances; hereafter such cases are not all given collation notes.
s0442.idiomatic: Rebelled-and-turned and rebelled-and-scattered are variant binomes of like sound and sense. The book uses turn and scatter interchangeably in several places; not every case is noted below.

s0443.literal: Ben fled toward Dian Che Lake: comment—the character "Che" should be "Che" (clear water).
s0443.idiomatic: On "Ben fled toward Dian Che Lake": Che should be Che (clear).

s0444.literal: The document conferring nine bestowments on Chen Baxian has the phrase "Xinchang and Dian Che, fully treading hardship"; an old collation says "'Dian Che' may originally have read 'Qu Che,' and the earlier 'Dian Che Lake' is the same."
s0444.idiomatic: The nine-bestowments text for Chen Baxian reads Xinchang and Dian Che, having fully borne hardship; old collation says Dian Che may have been Qu Che, as with Dian Che Lake above.

s0445.literal: Thus the edition seen by the old collation also read "Che."
s0445.idiomatic: The edition used by the old collation also read Che.

s0446.literal: That year was the first year of Taiqing: comment—according to the Annals of Emperor Wu in the Book of Liang, Li Ben's army collapsed in the first month of the first year of Zhongdatong, and he was killed in the third month of the second year of Taiqing.
s0446.idiomatic: On "that year was Taiqing year 1": the Book of Liang places Li Ben's rout in Zhongdatong 1/1 and his death in Taiqing 2/3.

s0447.literal: Li Qianshi entrusted himself to Dangyang: "entrusted" in all editions reads "promised."
s0447.idiomatic: On "Li Qianshi entrusted himself to Dangyang": all editions read promised for entrusted.

s0448.literal: The Hall edition's textual verification says: in one edition "promised" reads "entrusted."
s0448.idiomatic: The Hall edition notes one manuscript reads entrusted for promised.

s0451.idiomatic: says entrusted is the better reading.

s0452.literal: At the time the people of Ningdu, Liu Ai and others, supplied Qianshi with boats, armor, and weapons: "Liu Ai" in the Biographies of Du Sengming and Zhou Wenyu both read "Liu Xiaoshang"—are they one man with different names?
s0452.idiomatic: On "Liu Ai of Ningdu supplied Qianshi with ships and arms": Du Sengming's and Zhou Wenyu's biographies read Liu Xiaoshang—one person under two names?

s0453.literal: Sengbian's army halted at Pen city: "Pen" in the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Basin."
s0453.idiomatic: On "Sengbian halted at Pen city": the Southern History's Chen Wu annals read Basin.

s0454.literal: Comment: "Pen city" may be abbreviated as "Basin city"; the histories use the two graphs interchangeably—hereafter such cases are not all given collation notes.
s0454.idiomatic: Pen city may be shortened to Basin city; the histories interchange the two forms—not every case is noted below.

s0455.literal: The Founder with the various armies advanced and took Gushu: "Gushu" in the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions all read "Gushu" (with the mature graph).
s0455.idiomatic: On "took Gushu": Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions write Gushu with the mature character.

s0456.literal: Comment: the graphs shu and shu are the same; the histories also often interchange the two—hereafter such cases are not all given collation notes.
s0456.idiomatic: Shu and shu are the same character and often interchange in the histories—not every case is noted below.

s0457.literal: Jing's Commissioner Equal to the Three Dukes Lu Huilue opened Stone City's north gate and came over: "Lu Huilue" in the Biography of Hou Jing in the Book of Liang reads "Lu Huilue"; the Comprehensive Mirror agrees.
s0457.idiomatic: On "Lu Huilue opened Stone City's north gate and surrendered": the Book of Liang's Hou Jing biography and the Comprehensive Mirror read Lu Huilue.

s0458.literal: The Founder led the red out from Guangling to meet contingencies; when Jing's general Guo Yuanjian fled to Qi: the Taiping Imperial Overview 133 quotes, "The Founder led troops out from Guangling to meet Jing's general Guo Yuanjian; when Yuanjian fled to Qi"; the Yuan Gui 186 agrees—the sense is clearer; here there is omitted text.
s0458.idiomatic: On "the Founder led the red from Guangling": Taiping yulan 133 and Yuan Gui 186 read led troops to meet Guo Yuanjian, who then fled to Qi—clearer than the received text, which omits words.

s0459.literal: Xiang Province was pacified: the Hall edition's textual verification says, "The pacification of Xiang Province in the Book of Liang belongs to the affairs of the second year of Chengsheng."
s0459.idiomatic: On "Xiang Province pacified": the Hall edition places this in Chengsheng year 2 in the Book of Liang.

s0460.literal: Now examining the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties, this matter is placed in the second year of Chengsheng; the Comprehensive Mirror agrees; Yuan Gui 186 agrees.
s0460.idiomatic: The Southern History and Comprehensive Mirror date the pacification of Xiang Province to Chengsheng year 2; Yuan Gui 186 agrees.

s0461.literal: Imperial Overview 133 quotes above "Xiang Province pacified" the two characters "next year"—suspected omitted text here.
s0461.idiomatic: Taiping yulan 133 has next year before "Xiang Province pacified"—the main text may lack those words.

s0462.literal: In the third year, third month, the Founder was advanced to Grand Commandant: the Annals of Emperor Yuan in the Book of Liang reads "fourth month, guiyou"; the Comprehensive Mirror agrees.
s0462.idiomatic: On "year 3, month 3, advanced to Grand Commandant": the Book of Liang and Comprehensive Mirror read month 4, guiyou.

s0463.literal: Qi sent back the Marquis of Zhenyang Shen Ming to restore the altars of state: "Shen Ming" is "Yuan Ming"—changed to avoid the taboo of Tang Gaozu; the same below.
s0463.idiomatic: On "Qi returned Marquis of Zhenyang Shen Ming": Shen Ming stands for Yuan Ming, tabooed for Tang Gaozu—the same below.

s0465.literal: Yao Silian avoided the taboo of Tang Gaozu's grandfather; the character "bing" is everywhere changed to "jing"—hereafter such cases are not all given collation notes.
s0465.idiomatic: Yao Silian tabooed Tang Gaozu's grandfather and wrote jing for bing throughout—not every case is noted below.

s0466.literal: Chu Province Inspector Liu Shirong: the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties read "Liu Shirong."
s0466.idiomatic: On "Chu Inspector Liu Shirong": the Southern History's Chen Wu annals read Liu Shirong.

s0467.literal: Zhou Tiewu led naval forces cutting Qi transport: "Zhou Tiewu" is "Zhou Tiehu"—changed to avoid the taboo of Tang Gaozu's grandfather; the same below.
s0467.idiomatic: On "Zhou Tiewu cut Qi supply lines": Tiewu is Tiehu, tabooed for Tang Gaozu's grandfather—the same below.

s0468.literal: Going south to the province at Caishi: "Caishi" in the Southern Supervisory, Northern Supervisory, and Hall editions read "Caishi" (with the harvest graph).
s0468.idiomatic: On "south to Caishi": Southern, Northern Supervisory, and Hall editions write Caishi with the harvest character.

s0469.literal: Comment: the graphs cai and cai are the same; the histories also often interchange the two—hereafter such cases are not all given collation notes.
s0469.idiomatic: Cai and cai are the same character and often interchange—not every case is noted below.

s0470.literal: Luozhou Inspector Li Xiguang: Zhang Senkai
s0470.idiomatic: On "Luozhou Inspector Li Xiguang": Zhang Senkai

s0472.literal: says: "In the Biography of Gao Gan in the Book of Northern Qi, with the attached biography of his younger brother Jishi, it states that Li Xiguang in Northern Qi Tianbao served as Yangzhou inspector and, with Xiao Gui and others, crossed the river and died in battle—this differs from here."
s0472.idiomatic: says the Northern Qi biography of Gao Gan's brother Jishi makes Li Xiguang Yangzhou inspector under Tianbao, killed crossing the river with Xiao Gui—which disagrees with this passage.

s0473.literal: Outside the Grand Marshal gate at the White Beast stele slaughtered victims and reported to Heaven: "White Beast stele" is "White Tiger stele"—changed to avoid Tang taboo; the same below.
s0473.idiomatic: On "White Beast stele": White Beast is White Tiger, tabooed under Tang—the same below.

s0474.literal: Crossed the river to strike Qi Acting Commander Zhao Yan
s0474.idiomatic: Crossed the river to attack Qi acting commander Zhao Yan

s0476.literal: [Shen] at Guabu: corrected according to the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
s0476.idiomatic: [Shen] at Guabu: emended per the Southern History's Chen Wu annals.

s0477.literal: Comment: Zhao Yanshen has a biography in the Book of Northern Qi; the biography says his original name was Yin, and to avoid Qi temple taboo he went by his style.
s0477.idiomatic: Note: Zhao Yanshen's Northern Qi biography says his original name was Yin; he used his style to avoid Qi temple taboo.

s0478.literal: In antiquity personal names and styles corresponded—naturally to write "Shen" is correct.
s0478.idiomatic: Ancient name and style matched; Shen is the correct reading.

s0479.literal: That day the Son of Heaven mustered the feathered forest forbidden troops: "that day" in all editions reads "this day."
s0479.idiomatic: On "that day the emperor mustered the palace guard": all editions read this day for that day.

s0480.literal: Comment: that day is the same as this day—the graphs differ but the sense is the same.
s0480.idiomatic: That day and this day mean the same; only the graphs differ.

s0481.literal: Beheaded Liu Guiyi, Xu Siyan, and Fu Yenang in the Jiankang market: "Xu Siyan" in the Annals of the Deposed Emperor in the Book of Liang and the Annals of the Chen Emperor in the History of the Southern Dynasties both read "Xu Sichan."
s0481.idiomatic: On "beheaded Xu Siyan at Jiankang market": the Book of Liang's Deposed Emperor annals and the Southern History's Chen annals read Xu Sichan.

s0482.literal: An edict posthumously granted the Founder's elder brother Daotan Gentleman Attendant at the Palace: "Daotan" in the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions read "Daotan" (with speech); the original text of the lower scroll also reads "Daotan."
s0482.idiomatic: On "posthumously granted the Founder's brother Daotan Gentleman Attendant": Northern Supervisory, Jigu, Hall, and juan 2 read Daotan with the speech radical.

s0483.literal: Now because Tan and Tan are the same character, they are not normalized to one form.
s0483.idiomatic: Tan and Tan are treated as the same character and not forced to one spelling.

s0484.literal: Fief households each two thousand: comment—according to the biography of Prince Min of Nankang Tanlang, when Xiuxian was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Wukang county, the fief was one thousand households; afterward when posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Nankang commandery, he then received two thousand households.
s0484.idiomatic: On "fief two thousand households each": Prince Min of Nankang's biography gives Xiuxian one thousand households as Duke of Wukang and two thousand only as Prince of Nankang.

s0485.literal: This "two thousand households" should read "one thousand households."
s0485.idiomatic: Two thousand households here should be one thousand.

s0486.literal: Sent his generals Ouyang Wei, Fu Tai, and his son Zi as the vanguard army: comment—according to the Annals of the Deposed Emperor in the Book of Liang, Zi was Xiao Bo's younger brother's son; here it says "and his son Zi"—suspected omission of one character "younger brother's."
s0486.idiomatic: On "sent Ouyang Wei, Fu Tai, and his son Zi as vanguard": the Book of Liang makes Zi Bo's nephew; "his son" may lack younger brother's.

s0487.literal: Great Ultimate reaching Jiao and Yue: "Ultimate" in the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions read "Rescue."
s0487.idiomatic: On "Great Ultimate reaching Jiao and Yue": Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall read Rescue for Ultimate.

s0488.literal: Comment: ultimate is glossed as "reach"; "Great Ultimate" pairs with "far surpassing" above to form the text—writing "Ultimate" is correct.
s0488.idiomatic: Ultimate means reach; Great Ultimate pairs with far surpassing above—Ultimate is correct.

s0489.literal: "Dian Che" may originally have read "Qu Che"; the earlier "Dian Che Lake" is the same—all doubtful.
s0489.idiomatic: Dian Che may have been Qu Che, as with Dian Che Lake above—all uncertain.

s0490.literal: The Duke's dragon soar and tiger stride: comment—under Tang taboo avoidance, "tiger" is everywhere changed to "martial"; this "tiger" character is a later restoration.
s0490.idiomatic: On "dragon soar and tiger stride": Tang taboo changed tiger to martial; this tiger is a later restoration.

s0493.literal: [⓪]—corrected according to the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, Hall editions and the Southern History and Yuan Gui 186.
s0493.idiomatic: [⓪]—emended per Northern Supervisory, Jigu, Hall, Southern History, and Yuan Gui 186.

s0494.literal: Comment: "spirit chu" in the Southern Supervisory edition reads "spirit banner."
s0494.idiomatic: The Southern Supervisory edition reads spirit banner for spirit chu.

s0497.literal: [Sui] River and it did not flow: corrected according to the Southern Supervisory edition.
s0497.idiomatic: [Sui] River and it did not flow: emended per the Southern Supervisory edition.

s0498.literal: Comment: Yuan Gui 186 reads "Sui River"; the current Xiao Tong literary collection mostly reads "Si River."
s0498.idiomatic: Yuan Gui 186 reads Sui River; most received texts of Xu Ling's anthology read Si River.

s0499.literal: The Basic Annals of Gaozu in the Records of the Grand Historian has the phrase "the Sui River ceased to flow for it"—to write either "Sui River" or "Si River" is correct.
s0499.idiomatic: Shiji's Gaozu annals says the Sui River ceased to flow—either Sui or Si River is defensible.

s0500.literal: Outstanding heroic form: "heroic form" Yuan Gui 186 reads "heroic design"—suspected that "heroic design" is correct.
s0500.idiomatic: On "outstanding heroic form": Yuan Gui 186 reads heroic design, which may be correct.
